perspective:
**Alice Lim’s accessible information:**

- I know myself as Alice Lim, a dental hygienist. Austin Moreno is an old friend from high school; we remain close and often discuss our personal and professional lives. I know he works in insurance.
- I noticed Austin had become reserved when we talked about work. I suspected he might be hiding something about his job performance. I invited him for coffee and asked if things were okay at the office.
- Austin told me it was nothing, just the usual ups and downs; he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and said it was complicated.
- I told him he could talk to me.
- Afterward, I worried he might be dissatisfied and considering a career change. I asked if he had ever thought about changing careers.
- Austin said he had thought about it but didn’t know what other paths he could take and asked for suggestions.
- I suggested healthcare, offered to share my experiences, and said I could connect him with contacts. Austin said it sounded interesting and wanted to know more about my experiences and what it involves.
- I sensed he was hesitant because of fear of the unknown; I felt frustration and empathy. I told him about my friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and has never been happier.
- Austin said that was inspiring but he worried about the risks and initial struggle. I encouraged him that growth often comes from leaving comfort zones and that I support him. He thanked me and said my support and real success stories helped.
- I felt encouraged and hopeful by his openness. I suggested he talk to a career counselor and offered to connect him with friends in healthcare. Austin said that would be helpful and appreciated the connections. I said I would set up a meeting next week; he said he looked forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, I believed Austin was ready to take the next steps and appreciated my help. I felt satisfaction and joy. I told him I was proud and asked how he felt.
- Austin said he felt excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. I suggested regular check-ins. Austin agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that my perspective was valuable.
- I only know his work issues as he described them and as I inferred; I do not have direct access to his private thoughts or unspoken details.
